summary: Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as a Ministry of Education overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and held a post there as an expert researcher (attested 2026).

Yukihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn, held posts at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College (attested 1996–2015), and served as an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from circa 1953 to 1957 and later held a post there from circa 1970 to 2005.
Yukio Hattori (1932–2007) worked in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University from circa 1951 to 1955 and later held a post at Japan Women's University.

Yukio Kotani (born 1931) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. He served as an emeritus professor of comparative literature at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University. He was a professor at Toyo University (~1937–1969) and served as a professor, institute director, and president at Rissho University.

Yukio Takeda (1934–2021) specialized in history and archaeology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1961). He held posts at Nagoya City University, Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo (~1981–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.

Yukio Yamanaka works in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from the University of Freiburg, later holding posts at Ryukoku University and as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

Yuko Kamishima (born 1971) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned degrees from Indiana University Bloomington, Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at Waseda University (2006–2016) and Ritsumeikan University as professor in 2016.
Yuko Matsuda works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).
Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who earned an MA at the University of Tokyo and a PhD at the University of Groningen. She served as an associate professor at Kyoto University (attested 2002–2021).
Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, studying under supervisor Kirill Solonin and traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yumi Katayama works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

Yumi Nakamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Nakamoto studied at Ryukoku University as a graduate research student (attested 2014) and held a post there as an open-call researcher in 2012.
Yumiko Ishihama (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from circa 1981 to 1991 and held a post there around 2004.

Yumin Dai works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Dai studied at Hebei University, the University of Arizona, and earned a PhD from Nanjing University, where Dai became an assistant professor in 2019.

Yumzhana Zhabon is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied as a researcher at Saint Petersburg State University (1979–1985) and became a senior researcher at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies in 1985.

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Ji completed a PhD in Chinese literature at Fudan University in 2006 and held an attested post as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore in 2015.

Yung-Jong Shiah works in Buddhist and religious studies, earning a PhD at the University of Edinburgh (2003–2008). In 2025, Shiah was appointed Chair Professor and Dean of the College of Buddhist Studies at Fo Guang University.
